title: Scroll containers and scroll behaviour
learningObjectives: Explain scroll containers and scroll behaviour and use the relevant layout or responsive features.

understand.concept: A scroll container allows content to be scrolled within a box. overflow establishes scroll behaviour; scroll-behavior can request smooth programmatic scrolling; overscroll-behavior controls scroll chaining; scrollbar-gutter can reserve space for scrollbars in supported browsers.
understand.whyItMatters: Nested scroll regions can be difficult on touch devices and for keyboard users. Use them only when they improve the task, keep focus order logical, and avoid hiding important content.
understand.analogy: A scroll container is like a smaller window into a longer page; the reader needs a clear way to move through what is outside the window.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual scroll, sizing, and media-query behaviour follows browser layout rules.

explain.narrative: The feed scrolls within its own height. The tabindex makes the region focusable for keyboard scrolling.
